Broken Access Control: Inadequate restrictions on user actions and data access, often exacerbated by complex APIs and microservices.
Cryptographic Failures: Insecure transmission or storage of sensitive data (passwords, PII) due to weak/missing encryption.
Injection Attacks: Malicious input that manipulates SQL queries, OS commands, or API calls.
Insecure Design: Structural architectural flaws that, rather than implementation errors, fail to secure workflows.
Security Misconfigurations: Default credentials, unnecessary features, and misconfigured cloud buckets.
Vulnerable/Outdated Components: Continued, high-risk reliance on libraries/frameworks with known security holes.
Auth & Session Failures: Weak passwords and missing multi-factor authentication (MFA) allowing unauthorized access.
Software & Data Integrity Failures: Attacks on CI/CD pipelines and unsigned updates, such as in supply chain attacks.
Logging & Monitoring Failures: Inability to detect security breaches or monitor for malicious activity effectively.
Server-Side Request Forgery: Flaws allowing an attacker to force the server to make arbitrary requests to internal or external systems.
